$comment: TF-C75 (D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM) — THE DRIFT GUARD across the SEAM between the two observable faces of one fact. `Is bare char unsigned on this (architecture × object-format) pair?` shows up twice: (1) the CODEGEN face — the resolved signedness drives the SExt-vs-ZExt choice for the char→int promotion, so it is visible in what the program COMPUTES; and (2) the PREPROCESSOR face — the `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` predefine, visible to `#ifdef` before a single instruction is emitted. These are DECLARED SEPARATELY and can therefore DRIFT APART. The macro cannot be DERIVED from the resolved signedness by the engine: deriving it would mean naming `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` in engine code, a forbidden identity branch (the merge compares config strings to config strings and never hardcodes a macro name). So the seam is real and permanent, no agnostic engine-side coherence check is possible, and the anti-drift device must be THIS TEST. ★ DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED HERE: the config keys that carry either face. Their shape has already been reworked once and may be reworked again; this example must keep guarding the SEAM across any such rework, so it asserts only the two OBSERVABLES and never the spelling of the keys behind them. ★ WHY NO LEG IS VACUOUS: the exit code encodes BOTH observables independently — the macro in the tens digit, the emitted codegen in the units digit — so all four combinations are DISTINCT and the two drift states are unreachable by any correct configuration. exit 10 = macro says unsigned AND codegen zero-extends (COHERENT; correct on arm64×elf only); exit 1 = macro says signed AND codegen sign-extends (COHERENT; correct on every other shipped leg); exit 0 = macro says signed but codegen zero-extends (DRIFT — the macro predefine was lost or mis-gated, or the pair stopped resolving to signed); exit 11 = macro says unsigned but codegen sign-extends (DRIFT — the macro predefine leaked onto a signed-`char` leg). 0 and 11 are wrong on EVERY leg, and on any given leg exactly one of {1, 10} is right, so no single-sided edit can restore green: dropping the macro predefine turns the elf leg 10 → 0, leaking it onto macho turns that leg 1 → 11, and making the config resolve arm64 × macho back to unsigned turns it 1 → 0. ★ THE FIRST TWO OF THOSE WERE MEASURED BY THIS AGENT, NOT ASSUMED: perturbing the config to ungate the macro predefine made the macho leg fail its `#error` leg loudly (compiler rc=1), and with that one `#error` neutered in a scratch copy of main.c the same perturbed config produced EXIT 11 — the drift value predicted above; deleting the predefine outright made the arm64 × elf leg fail its `#error` leg (compiler rc=1). Both perturbations were reverted. The `volatile` seed keeps the byte a RUNTIME value so the units digit is the real machine char→int extension (sxtb/ldrsb vs uxtb/ldrb) in the baseline AND the `release` arm, never a const-fold. ★ THE COMPILE-TIME `#error` LEGS IN main.c ARE NOT REDUNDANT WITH THESE EXIT CODES: only the arm64:macho64 row actually EXECUTES on a darwin host (the runner compiles the other three, then reports that their `runOn` excludes host=darwin), so without them the arm64×ELF half — the ONLY leg where `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` is defined, i.e. the entire point of the macro — would be INERT on the only host that can run it. The `#error` legs are checked at COMPILE time on every leg, so all four are verified on any host. ★ RELATION TO THE STANDING CONSTRAINT in examples/c/arch_identity_predefines/main.c (do not build a runtime ARCHITECTURE cross-check on bare-`char` signedness): that constraint still holds and must not be spread into unrelated examples. This is not that — it is a SELF-CONSISTENCY check between two declarations of ONE fact, not an attempt to identify a machine, and self-consistency is the only way to catch this drift. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 (Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64, Apple clang 21.0.0 / clang-2100.1.1.101 via /usr/bin/clang; DSS built from this tree), every exit code captured DIRECTLY, never after a pipe: (a) `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null` DEFINES __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1 for -target aarch64-linux-gnu and does NOT define it for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc or x86_64-apple-darwin; (b) DSS AGREES ON ALL FOUR SHIPPED LEGS, probed with #ifdef/#ifndef + #error and the compiler's exit code captured directly — DEFINED (and == 1) on arm64:elf64-aarch64-linux-exec, NOT DEFINED on arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec, x86_64:elf64-x86_64-linux-exec and x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec; (c) `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` compiles clean (rc 0 ⇒ SIGNED) for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and FAILS (rc 1 ⇒ UNSIGNED) for aarch64-linux-gnu; (d) THIS main.c passes `clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra` clean for all four triples, i.e. every `#error` leg is satisfied under clang too; (e) THIS main.c, clang-built and run NATIVELY, exits 1 at -O0 AND 1 at -O2.

targets.$comment: ★ THE ONLY LEG WHERE `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` IS DEFINED — and therefore the only row whose value is 10 rather than 1. Bare `char` IS unsigned on aarch64-linux-gnu, so BOTH observables say unsigned: the macro is defined (tens digit 1) AND the codegen zero-extends, making `(char)0x80 < 0` false (units digit 0) ⇒ 1*10 + 0 = 10. This row is what gives the guard its power: it is the one place the two declarations must BOTH flip together, so it is the one place drift shows up. If this row ever reads 0, the macro predefine was lost or mis-gated; if it reads 11, the codegen half regressed to sign-extending; if it reads 1, BOTH went wrong in the same direction, i.e. the arm64 × elf pair had silently stopped resolving to unsigned. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28: `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target aarch64-linux-gnu` DEFINES __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1; DSS defines it (and == 1) on this exact spec, probed with #ifdef/#ifndef + #error with the compiler exit code captured directly; `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` FAILS (rc 1 ⇒ unsigned) for that triple. The RUN itself was NOT executed on this host (this is a linux/aarch64 image and no qemu-aarch64 is installed here); the 10 is derived from those two independently MEASURED halves, and the compile-time `#error` legs in main.c verify the macro half of it on THIS host at every build.

arm64 × macho — the leg this anchor was opened for, and the only one that actually EXECUTES on a darwin host. Apple's platform ABI chose SIGNED `char`, so BOTH observables say signed: `__CHAR_UNSIGNED__` is NOT defined (tens digit 0) AND the codegen sign-extends, making `(char)0x80 < 0` true (units digit 1) ⇒ 0*10 + 1 = 1. Note this is the SAME 1 as the two x86_64 rows but reached differently: on x86_64 the CPU default is already signed, whereas here the AArch64 CPU default of UNSIGNED is overridden to signed for the macho pair, while the macro predefine is held off this leg by its object-format gate. Both halves are load-bearing and this row fails distinctly if either goes: make the config resolve this pair to unsigned again and it returns 0; leak the macro predefine onto macho and it returns 11. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64, every exit code captured DIRECTLY (never after a pipe): DSS does NOT define __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ on this spec (probed with #ifdef/#ifndef + #error); Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) compiled this exact main.c and ran it natively → exit 1 at -O0 AND exit 1 at -O2; DSS compiled the same file for arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec and ran it → exit 1 in the baseline arm AND exit 1 under the `release` arm. DSS and clang agree.
